components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview:
The portfolio behaves like a carefully edited casebook whose evidence is actively being examined, connected, and explained. It pairs the authority and pacing of an independent design journal with the precision of a product walkthrough. The page is expressive through scale, sequencing, and selective asymmetry—not through ornament.

The visual system is warm, modern, and technically credible. Large editorial moments draw visitors into the work; disciplined sans-serif typography, a visible grid, concise metadata, and structured process content make the material easy to evaluate. The experience must never drift into ecommerce, luxury-campaign, wedding-brand, vintage-stationery, or generic AI-startup conventions.
keyCharacteristics: Expressive editorial composition with controlled asymmetry
Warm paper-like neutrals and a scarce oxblood accent
Selective serif identity paired with highly readable bilingual sans-serif text
Varied media scale, generous whitespace, and clear evidence hierarchy
Flat, precise surfaces with minimal decoration and strong accessibility

rules.name: The Red-Pencil Rule
rules.body: Oxblood marks actions, selection, sequence, and emphasis; it never carries long paragraphs or dominates large background regions.

rules.name: The Paper Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Warm Ivory is the page; Paper White is a purposeful content layer. Do not alternate them mechanically section by section.

rules.name: The Serif Is a Signal Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif identifies major narrative thresholds and selected work; it is never used for long paragraphs, dense controls, small labels, or complex navigation.

rules.name: The Bilingual Measure Rule
rules.body: English and Thai share hierarchy and intent, not forced line breaks or identical element heights. Containers flex to the reviewed translation.

rules.name: The Flat Evidence Rule
rules.body: Content earns prominence through scale and placement. Shadows do not substitute for hierarchy.

dos: Do let selected case-study evidence lead the visual hierarchy.
Do use large editorial typography selectively and scale it responsibly on mobile.
Do use asymmetry to express priority while preserving a clear reading order.
Do vary image scale and content density to distinguish case studies from activities and achievements.
Do use Oxblood Annotation sparingly for action, navigation state, numbering, links, and precise highlights.
Do maintain visible focus, strong contrast, semantic structure, reduced-motion support, and flexible bilingual layouts.
Do label placeholders, synthetic demonstrations, and unconfirmed content honestly.
donts: Don't reproduce ecommerce navigation, product grids, shop cards, badges, or category merchandising.
Don't use gradients, neon glow, glassmorphism, continuous animation, excessive shadows, or generic AI-startup imagery.
Don't use nested cards, unnecessary decorative icons, ornamental vintage treatments, floral motifs, or stationery styling.
Don't use Oxblood for long body copy or as an indiscriminate background.
Don't set long paragraphs, small labels, dense interface text, or complex navigation in the serif face.
Don't use low-contrast secondary text, overly thin serif weights, oversized mobile headings, or fixed-height text containers.
